text:
Ajay: Seeing a sudden 40% throughput drop across a subset of dedicated nodes in eu-west-1, started ~20m ago. p95 latency up from 120ms -> 560ms. Many worker restarts.
Maria: +1, alerts fired for cluster-2023-gpupool, noise in kernel-selection metrics. Any OOM logs?
Kevin: grabbing logs now, looks like repeated CUDA OOMs then worker PID exits. Example from node-7: 
```
2026-03-18T09:41:12Z worker[2378]: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 16.00 GiB total capacity; 12.3 GiB already allocated)
2026-03-18T09:41:12Z worker[2378]: terminating due to signal 6
```
Tara: Not all tenants affected. Noisy-tenant heuristic flagged high small-batch rate on node-7 earlier. Could be fragmentation + frequent small allocations.
Ajay: Can we profile allocator to see slab usage / free list fragmentation? Also check KV cache evict churn.
Kevin: Ran quick kvcache stats: `kvcache.evictions.rate` spiked from 30/s -> 700/s on node-7. KV shard sizes oscillating between 200MB and 3.1GB.
Maria: If KV cache thrashing then kernel selection fallback could be firing (fastpath -> safe paths) triggering bigger allocations per request. Check kernel-routing logs.
Kevin: Extracted kernel-routing trace for a flapping request id: `KR[route_id=0x9f3] -> fallback to generic-attn` 23 times in 5m. Usually we see 0-1.
Oncall: Rolling drain of node-7 in progress (kubectl cordon/drain). Taking it out of load to stop restart loop. ETA 6m. :mechanical_arm:
Ajay: Good. In parallel, can we hotpatch allocator flags to enable slab compaction more aggressively? `ALLOCATOR_COMPACT=1` exists on next runtime but needs restart to pick up. Hotpatch via env toggle?
Tara: We have an interim knob: `SLOWPATH_EVICT_THRESHOLD` can be bumped to reduce eviction churn. Pushed `SLOWPATH_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6` on node-7 for testing.
Kevin: After cordon + knob change, kv evictions down to ~90/s and restarts stopped. Throughput climbed to ~85% of baseline in 10m. p95 improved to ~220ms.
Maria: Great. We still have memory fragmentation in metrics: `gpu.mem.frag_ratio` averaged 0.47 on node-7 vs 0.12 on healthy nodes. That matches repeated small allocations. Need longer-term: better batching heuristics + prefetch alignment.
Ajay: Action items: 1) mark node-7 as flaky and exclude from scheduling until we do a full sweep (Kevin). 2) Run a profiler job to capture slab distribution and kernel-call patterns across 1h window (Tara). 3) Short-term: add eviction threshold change to rollout for impacted pool (Maria). 4) Postmortem with root cause -> likely KV thrash + kernel fallback amplification (Ajay).
Oncall: Noted. For now we reverted `SLOWPATH_EVICT_THRESHOLD` cluster-wide to 0.6 on the other 2 affected nodes; monitoring.
Kevin: Uploading profiler snapshot to S3: s3://redwood-internal/profiler/2138001234/ — contains allocator histograms, kernel-choice timeline, and per-tenant batch size distribution.
Tara: Quick note from trace: many requests fell back to `generic-attn` when `seq_len > 512` combined with small-batch bursts. Batching heuristic didn't merge bursty single-token requests because latency SLOs set to conservative 25ms, so we elected to run as-is and ended up with many tiny allocations. Need to tune `min_batch_delay` for these queues.
Maria: Agreed. For the postmortem let's quantify how much fallback kernels increased per-token GPU working set. If it's >15% we can justify kernel routing hotfix.
Ajay: I'll schedule follow-up investigation meeting 11:00 UTC and own the postmortem. For now incident status: mitigated (partial), nodes cordoned, defangs applied. Will update channel when we move to resolved. :white_check_mark:
